explanation: I found no Mathlib declaration that states this. The theorem says that if T is reduced and the range of u lies in the closure of the range of f (f quasi-compact), then f.ker ≤ u.ker. In Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Basic.lean I found Hom.ker_apply, Hom.le_ker_comp, Hom.support_ker (f.ker.support = closure (range f)), Hom.range_subset_ker_support and ker_of_isAffine. In Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean I found the closed-immersion lift lemma, which takes f.ker ≤ g.ker as a hypothesis. None of these concludes f.ker ≤ u.ker from a closure-of-range condition with T reduced. Searches for ker_le_ker, basicOpen_inter_closure and eq_zero_of_basicOpen_eq_bot, and for lemmas relating ker to IsReduced, turned up nothing relevant in Mathlib. The proof here uses Scheme.Hom.basicOpen_inter_closure_range_eq_empty. That lemma is not in Mathlib, so it is presumably another declaration of this library. Getting the result from Hom.support_ker would also need an argument of some substance, not a one- or two-line derivation.
